**Best fit: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2.** Its 2,600 W inverter gives comfortable headroom for a typical single-burner induction cooktop, which can draw up to 1,800 W, and for a kettle whose label is below 2,600 W. It has a 2,073.6 Wh battery, so it can handle the load; how long it runs depends on the appliance and heat setting. [Specs and buying link](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop)

For comparison, the key is **continuous AC output**, not just battery size: look for at least 1,800 W for a full-power induction burner. [Induction cooktop power guide](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/induction-cooktop/) A litre of water takes roughly 90–110 Wh to boil, so the battery should manage multiple boils, though actual count will be lower after conversion losses. ([Source](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop))
